faqs.q: How do you tell storm damage from normal roof wear?

runs.v: Storm damage usually shows up as sudden, isolated issues after a specific weather event: lifted or missing shingles, punctures from debris, dented flashing, torn membrane seams on flat roofs, or fresh water intrusion in the attic or ceiling. Normal wear tends to look more even and gradual, such as general granule loss, aging sealant, or long-term brittleness. A roof inspection helps confirm whether the damage is recent, weather-related, and likely to support an insurance claim.

faqs.q: What is the deadline to file a storm-damage roof claim in New Jersey?

runs.v: Claim deadlines depend on your insurance policy, so the safest move is to document the damage and report it as soon as possible after the storm. Waiting can make it harder to show what the storm caused versus what happened later from continued exposure or delayed maintenance. If you are not sure where to start, we can inspect the roof, document visible storm-related issues, and help you understand what information your insurer may request.

faqs.q: Can storm damage be repaired, or does the roof need full replacement?

runs.v: That depends on the extent and location of the damage. Localized issues, such as a limited section of missing shingles or flashing damage, can often be repaired without replacing the entire roof. If the storm has affected a large area, compromised an older roofing system, or allowed water to reach the decking or framing, the scope may go beyond surface repairs. We inspect the full roof system so you know whether a targeted repair is enough or whether replacement is the more reliable long-term option.

faqs.q: How much does storm damage roof repair cost in Essex County, NJ?

runs.v: The cost depends on the roofing material, how widespread the damage is, how easy the roof is to access, and whether the issue is limited to the outer roofing layer or has led to structural damage from ongoing leaks. Small repairs may be relatively straightforward, while larger storm-related work or partial reconstruction will cost more. Delaying service can raise the total if water keeps getting in, so the best first step is a professional inspection and written estimate.

faqs.q: Does an impact-resistant roof reduce storm damage and claims?

runs.v: Impact-resistant materials can help reduce damage from hail and wind-driven debris, but they do not make a roof storm-proof. Performance still depends on the roofing system, installation quality, roof age, and the severity of the storm. For some properties, upgraded materials may improve durability and reduce the likelihood of repeated repairs, but they should be chosen based on the building type and roof design.

faqs.q: What time of year do most roof storms hit New Jersey?

runs.v: New Jersey roofs can take storm hits in every season. Summer often brings strong thunderstorms, wind, and heavy rain, while winter creates its own problems through snow, ice, and repeated freezing and thawing. Newark typically experiences 30-50 freeze-thaw cycles each winter, and those repeated shifts can turn small storm openings into larger leak problems if they are not sealed promptly.

faqs.q: Can winter storms cause roof leaks even if no shingles blew off?

runs.v: Yes. Ice dams form when heat escapes a poorly insulated attic, which melts snow on the roof and lets water refreeze at the colder edges. That backed-up water can work under shingles and create leak risk after winter storms, even when the roof looks mostly intact from the ground.
